latency_note: StreamLAAL reduces to LAAL on sentence-level data: its extra mwerSegmenter step aligning an unsegmented hypothesis stream to reference sentences is the identity when each item is already one sentence. The paper reports RealSI LAAL only in Figures 3/4 (no numeric table) and StreamLAAL only on long-form ACL60/60-dev Figure 5, so latency cannot be placed beside it.

latency.ap_not_usable: SimulEval AP assumes len(delays) and reference_length share units; our delays are per speech chunk (5.5-5.9) against a reference length in chars/words (tens), so AP lands at 0.04-0.25 rather than anywhere meaningful. AL/LAAL/DAL are unaffected.
latency.first_audible_definitions: Two distinct quantities, both reported and not to be mixed: StartOffset is the first fragment's emission time (the internal reports' 首次发音 / first_emission_ms; it equals delays[0] because the first fragment never queues), while 真实可听起始 is audio_quality.leading_silence_ms -- the first voiced frame of the placed audio, energy-based.  For C at k1 they are 2544/2573 ms and 4720/4720 ms respectively.

m3_control.why: m3's published latency was measured on trajectory.events, the gold event list.  Over 3000 gold trajectories / 42108 events the gold events are a median 0.429 of the available 160 ms read points (p10 0.327, p90 0.562), 15.8% admit no new audio, and their boundaries are the gold word boundaries -- oracle segmentation.  run_event reads only source_glm_start/end, source_end_ms and source_final, so the policy is genuinely free-running; it is the read schedule that is gold.
shared_with_c: WhisperVQ frontend and its GLM embedding math
m3_control.differs: weights, and the runtime those weights were trained for
m3_control.m3_config: its own gate: pace margin 1200 ms, tail 2000 ms, cap 384, 4 fragments, 48 text tokens
m3_control.pacer_ruled_out: margin 1200 -> 2000 moves ASR-BLEU by 0.11 / 0.03, leaves first-audible identical to the millisecond and the audible count unchanged; the first fragment's median 127/164 tokens sits under its 200-token budget, so onset was never pace-limited.
m3_control.low_internal_silence_is_an_artifact: m3 emits a median 2 fragments against C's 5, its first fragment is a median 127/164 tokens (2.5-3.3 s of speech in one dump), and the internal-silence median counts only voiced files -- so m3's 22-26% fully silent samples never enter it.  Fewer, larger, later blobs, not smoother streaming.
m3_control.RETRACTED_attribution: The claim that m3's low published latency was caused by oracle segmentation (the gold read schedule) is WITHDRAWN.  An isolation run over the same 80 internal gold samples with the same weights, session and scorers, changing only the read schedule, gives LAAL 3466 (gold) vs 3221 (uniform 160 ms) and first-audible 2087 vs 1972, with 69/80 vs 75/80 samples emitting -- the blind grid is slightly BETTER and the effect is near zero in the opposite direction. The gold events are genuinely oracle-aligned (a median 0.429 of the available 160 ms read points, 15.8% admitting no new audio) but that does not move latency.

c_source_asr_by_read_step.note: The mechanism behind the asymmetric quality-latency cost in section 6: C's Chinese source ASR collapses at a fine read step while English barely moves.  Same punctuation-stripped code across all three arms.

factors_ranked.factor: metric delay axis (per-token latency_family -> per-fragment SimulEval)
factors_ranked.why: latency_family's laal_step is source_duration/max(hyp_units, reference).  With per-token delays hyp_units is ~290 so the step is ~20.7 ms on a 6 s utterance while the delays themselves grow at exactly 20 ms per token -- the subtraction cancels the growth and LAAL degenerates to 'when speech starts'.  With per-fragment delays there are 3-5 points, the reference length is in chars/words (tens), the step is ~190 ms and the fragments are 1-2 s apart, so LAAL becomes 'when speech chunks arrive on average'. Two different questions, not two measurements of one quantity.

LAAL is near-linear in source length: 1349 ms at 0-3 s, 1963 at 3-5 s, 3570 at 5-7 s, 5101 at 7-10 s (same arm, same metric, same schedule).  Median duration was 3700 ms for the gate 6, 5530 ms for the 80 panel, 6470 ms for RealSI.

The published 883 ms first-audible came from streaming_demos_delta5's two short demos.  On the 80-sample panel they rank 1st and 6th fastest of 69 emitting samples (320 and 480 ms against a panel median of 1440 and p90 of 4320).  Reporting only the fastest k gives first-audible 320 ms at k=2 and 2087 ms at k=69.  Dominant for the 883 ms figure; only 0.86x on LAAL.
The blind grid is slightly better.  Retracted as an explanation.

factors_ranked.factor: data domain (internal reconstructions -> RealSI real recordings)
factors_ranked.why: In the 5000-7000 ms bucket m3 scores LAAL 3104 internally and 3187 on RealSI, a 2.7% difference.  The domain costs quality (ASR-BLEU 1.73/0.80) but almost no latency.

why_m3_latency_grew.rule: LAAL moves by multiples when the delay axis granularity, the sample set or the source-duration distribution change, so any cross-report LAAL comparison must first state whether all three match.  This project's internal history uses the per-token axis; comparison against the paper requires the per-fragment axis.  The two must never be mixed, and the old internal figures are not evidence that latency used to be better.

m3_delta5_correction.what_was_wrong: The earlier m3 arms used delta=0, m3's gate configuration.  m3's own streaming_demos_delta5/FINDINGS.zh-CN.md calls CONTINUE_WRITE_BIAS=5 the best streaming S2ST configuration in the whole project (5/6 gate criteria against 3/6 at delta=0) because it lifts WRITE_MT per event from 0.168 to 0.789.  Comparing C against delta=0 compared it against a configuration m3's authors set aside.
m3_delta5_correction.installation_validated: install_bias(0,5) at runtime, no m3 file touched; measured WRITE_MT/event 0.774 on 80 samples against the documented 0.789 on 16.
m3_delta5_correction.verdict: m3 at delta=5 is 3-8x faster on first-audible and LAAL; C is 10-20x better on content.  A real trade-off, not one side dominating.  delta=5 costs m3 6 BLEU on internal data but nothing on RealSI, because its RealSI quality is already at the floor (BLEU ~1).

oracle_segmentation_buys_asr_not_latency.note: Completes the earlier retraction: the gold schedule does help m3, but in recognition, not latency.

c_onset_diagnosis.method: onset_diagnosis.py reads trace.source_deltas / target_deltas (one committed-character count per read step) and Fragment.read_step, on the 80-sample internal panel at a 160 ms read step.
c_onset_diagnosis.key_finding: speech onset equals the MT committer's first release in 80/80 samples at every holdback, so TTS adds no delay at all; the entire onset is the ASR->MT commit chain.
c_onset_diagnosis.conclusion: Of the 2080 ms onset, 960 ms is the ASR committer and a further 1120 ms is the MT committer -- the MT half is the larger one.  Zero commit conflicts at every setting, so the holdback is pure conservatism rather than conflict avoidance.  s1t0, which was never tried before (only s0t1 and s2t1 were), buys 480 ms for 2.2/4.4 BLEU with the ASR error unchanged -- a 2.7x better exchange rate than s0t0's 960 ms for 11.9/11.5 BLEU.  So release the target committer, never the source committer.
c_onset_diagnosis.real_fix: Train the ASR stage on a uniform fine read grid.  C's Chinese source CER is 0.250 offline, 0.264 at k25 and 0.804 at k1 while English barely moves (0.363/0.390/0.421); m3 shows the same failure worse (0.248 -> 1.708); third-party ASR reads the same audio at 0.141/0.159 so the audio is fine; and because the onset is ASR-commit-bound, a better ASR agrees sooner and buys latency and quality together instead of trading them.  This is the only lever that improves both.
c_onset_diagnosis.what_will_not_work: A delta-style unconditional write.  m3 at delta=5 already walked that path to its end: 347 ms onset at ASR-BLEU 1.36, WER 1.75 and 1.8x text over-generation.

audible_onset_correction.what_was_wrong: Reported 真实可听起始 values added delays[0] to audio_quality.leading_silence_ms, double-counting.  leading_silence_ms is measured on the already-placed audio, so it is absolute: verified delays[0]=2240 against leading_silence=2440, the extra ~200 ms being the synthesized fragment's own head silence. The correct quantity is leading_silence_ms alone, which is what m3style.py used for the published 883/978 ms figures.
audible_onset_correction.effect_on_conclusions: Directions unchanged everywhere except one: on the internal panel C and m3 delta=0 go from 'C worse by 730 ms' to essentially tied (2620 against 2600).  On RealSI C still beats m3 delta=0 (by 620/680 ms rather than the reported 750/1040) and m3 delta=5 still beats C by 4.6x/3.7x.
audible_onset_correction.two_onset_quantities: StartOffset is the first speech chunk's emission time (SimulEval aggregate); 真实可听起始 is the first voiced frame of the placed audio (energy-based, median).  They are different questions and the master table now reports StartOffset, its median, and the energy onset side by side so they can be read against each other.

master_table.note: Every metric this project tracks, all six operating points, one dataset, one code path.

next_steps.comparability: Valid as an operating-point comparison on a public benchmark -- the 777 frozen segments, the 160 ms read grid, the WhisperVQ frontend and its GLM embedding math, the BiCodec decoder, the timeline placement, the SimulEval scorers, the ASR-BLEU chain and the common ancestor checkpoint are all shared.  Not valid as a comparison of training recipes: the runtimes differ (isolated cascade with task prefixes against one interleaved session with decision tokens), neither model was ever trained on a uniform 160 ms grid, they degrade off-distribution by different amounts (m3's ASR 0.248 -> 1.708, C's Chinese 0.264 -> 0.804), and the knob spaces are asymmetric -- m3 has delta because it has decision tokens, C structurally has none and its analogue is the committer holdback.
next_steps.verdict: On RealSI, C, decisively: m3 scores ASR-BLEU 0.5-1.9 at any delta, and a BLEU of 1 is not a translation, so the latency of a non-translation is not a latency achievement.  But this is a statement about RealSI, not about m3 in general: on m3's own internal domain with the gold schedule, m3 at delta=5 is a genuine Pareto point (MT text BLEU 18/14 at LAAL 1401 against C's 39/33 at LAAL 3667).  The public benchmark is the one that counts.

s1t0_adopted.recommendation: make s1t0 the default: about a second of onset for under 0.7 BLEU

decisive_finding.statement: On the samples where C's source ASR already works (error < 0.15), C k25 scores 25.66 En->Zh and 21.12 Zh->En -- at or above the paper's m=4 of 25.54 and near its 22.47. C's translation and synthesis are not worse than the paper's; the entire gap is the source ASR error distribution.

priority: DONE: adopt s1t0 as the default (config only, no training)

The one training run worth opening: pure CE plus an ASR family on a uniform 160 ms read grid, Chinese source weighted up.  Target k1 Chinese CER 0.804 -> about 0.26.  Four measurements agree on it, and it is the only lever that buys latency and quality together, because the onset is committer-bound and a better ASR agrees sooner.  Bucket analysis sizes the payoff at +8.3/+6.7 BLEU.
Then length matching (bp 0.79-0.83), worth +3.6/+2.3.  Terminator rate is already 1.000, so the shortfall is committed text volume, not END timing.

Explicitly not: a delta-style unconditional write (m3 walked it to 347 ms at BLEU 1.36); pacer tuning (the margin 1200<->2000 control proves it is a no-op); TTS work in isolation (measured to contribute zero onset, and C's peak 0.776-0.859 and >4kHz 0.003 already match or beat m3).

laal_is_mostly_chunk_count.formula: LAAL = mean(d_i) - step*(N-1)/2 with step = source_duration/max(N, reference_length); N is the speech-chunk count, so a larger N subtracts more, independently of when audio actually arrives.
laal_is_mostly_chunk_count.consequence: After s1t0 C's audio arrives on average only 413-556 ms later than m3 at delta=5, while LAAL reports 2219-3120 ms later.  Treating LAAL as the headline latency number at these operating points was inaccurate on my part; it is mostly chunk-count driven here.  It also means C could cut LAAL sharply by fragmenting each committed lump into smaller chunks without the audio arriving any earlier -- that is gaming the metric, so it must not be done, and LAAL must always be reported next to StartOffset and mean(d) so it is not misread.

real_gap_is_first_audible.note: s1t0 recovered 800 ms; 1120 ms remain against m3 at delta=5, and this number carries no formula term.

commit_rate_is_the_bound.mechanism: C speaks on about 1 read step in 8, and that is not policy conservatism -- releasing the target holdback moves it only 0.111 -> 0.133.  It is the source word rate: the ASR committer releases a word, MT re-translates, MT's LCP grows by a phrase, TTS speaks a phrase.  A 45-step utterance holds about a dozen words and therefore about a dozen release cycles.  m3 at delta=5 breaks that bound by writing MT at every event whether or not the source grew, i.e. by composing ahead of the audio, and the table shows the price: source ASR error 1.48, 1.8x text over-generation, ASR-BLEU 1.36.

untried_cheap_experiment.name: word-boundary commit
untried_cheap_experiment.what: The ASR committer trims a fixed number of characters off the agreed prefix (LCP(previous, current) - holdback).  Releasing up to the last complete word instead would release earlier at the same risk, and the effect should be largest on English sources where trimming one character differs a lot from trimming to a word boundary.
untried_cheap_experiment.not_the_same_as: SeededPrefixCommitter, which seeded `previous` on the first call and measured worse; word-level trimming has never been tried.

m3_error_attribution.question: m3 at delta=5+rp1.1 sounds smooth but translates wrongly -- is it ASR, incremental MT or TTS?
m3_error_attribution.answer: ASR and TTS, with the interleaved architecture as a distinct fourth loss.  Incremental MT is innocent.

tts_fidelity_whisper_vs_own_text.m3_d5_rp13_note: Whisper rejected it as implausible_after_single_item_retry, so rp=1.3 is worse for m3 than its own choice of 1.1 despite also zeroing the spectral freeze

m3_own_gate_16_samples.reading: With ASR error at only 0.037 on cmn, MT capability given gold source is 27.67/35.86 -- above the offline teacher measured the same way -- yet the same weights and the same ASR input collapse from 17.51 to 0.10 once MT runs inside the interleaved session rather than as a standalone incremental rollout.  The interleaved session gates MT behind a decision token (WRITE_MT per event 0.147 at delta=0, coverage 0.295) and interleaves semantic TTS tokens into the same KV cache, polluting the context the MT continuation reads.  Confirmed incidentally this session: adding a repetition penalty, which touches only semantic decoding, changed the MT text too.

m3_error_attribution.implication_for_c: C is structurally immune to the fourth loss -- three isolated cascade stages, MT with its own task prefix and a clean context, no shared continuation with TTS.  That explains a 10-20x ASR-BLEU advantage on RealSI between two models whose gold-source MT is comparable.  C's TTS fidelity is 0.706 against m3's 0.304, spectral freeze 0.000 and >4 kHz 0.004.  C's one remaining large problem is still the source ASR -- a fourth independent line of evidence pointing at the same fix.
